mi_aaa_wall.blurb: A small bolted crag in the hills north of Marquette, roughly a quarter hour from the village of Big Bay, reached by a chain of lightly signed dirt and gravel roads. It holds about 25 climbs, most of them sport leads, with a handful of top-rope setups and a few trad lines. Difficulty runs from easy fourth-class-feeling 5.4 through to a single 5.13, but the bulk sits between 5.9 and 5.10, so it suits climbers with a few seasons of leading behind them as well as newer ones looking for moderates. A separate older top-rope wall and a shorter satellite crag sit close by.

mi_cliff_s_ridge_aka_marquette_mtn.blurb: A single-pitch quartzite face of around 70 feet just south of Marquette, up on the ridge above the ski hill. Most of the 23 climbs here are set up as top-ropes, with a smaller number of trad leads on cracks and overhanging steps. Grades start near 5.4 and top out in the low 5.11s, though the heart of the crag is 5.7 to 5.10. The rock offers good friction. There are no bolts, so anchors come from slinging trees with long webbing or static line, and a trad rack helps for the crack lines. A short trail leads around the left side of the cliff to reach the top.
mi_cliff_s_ridge_aka_marquette_mtn.parking_note: Drive south-southwest from Marquette on County Road 553, turn onto the dirt road just beyond the round house, and leave the car by the radio tower maintenance buildings or in the small lot next to them.
mi_cliff_s_ridge_aka_marquette_mtn.approach: A trail heads northeast from the second lot to the base of the rock.

ma_auburn_ice_canyon.blurb: A winter-only ice venue in Auburn, just off Route 20 and a short drive from Worcester, built in a manmade drainage channel. Roughly twenty climbs, mostly water ice with a couple of mixed lines, run up to nearly 100 feet. Most of the ice is around WI3, with a few easier flows and a few steeper pitches near WI4, so it works as both a practice spot for newcomers and a quick fix for people who do not want the long haul north. The canyon floor can hold water, which makes conditions vary from week to week, and it tends to draw a crowd on good weekends.

mn_annadonia_area.blurb: A section of the south-facing bluff above the Mississippi at Red Wing, tucked beside Sunburst Buttress and directly beneath the end of the summit hiking trail. Around 28 climbs, nearly all of them bolted sport routes with a very small amount of trad and top-rope. Difficulty reaches from 5.7 to 5.13, though most of the routes fall between 5.9 and 5.11, and a popular lower-angle warm-up wall near the start gets many first ties of the day. Routes can be up to about 80 feet. Expect crowds, sandy and sometimes loose rock, and visitors above who may knock things down, so a helmet is wise.
